SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #12
====

GRADE: Grade 6
SUBJECT: SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Overgrazing continuously
   B. Burning crop residue every week
   C. Removing all vegetation
   D. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

2. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water removes heat too quickly
   B. Petrol fires have no fuel
   C. Water always increases oxygen
   D. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

3. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Light? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Light.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Light.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Light.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Light.

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Levers as simple machines? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Levers as simple machines.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Levers as simple machines.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Levers as simple machines.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Levers as simple machines.

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Slopes as simple machines? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Slopes as simple machines.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Slopes as simple machines.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Slopes as simple machines.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Slopes as simple machines.

6. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. joule (J)
   B. watt (W)
   C. pascal (Pa)
   D. newton (N)

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Invertebrates? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Invertebrates.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Invertebrates.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Invertebrates.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Invertebrates.

8. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 50 °C
   B. 100 °C
   C. 37 °C
   D. 0 °C

9. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only carbon dioxide
   B. Glucose and oxygen
   C. Nitrogen gas only
   D. Only water vapour

10. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Movement of water only across a membrane
   B. Heating until a solid melts
   C. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   D. A chemical reaction forming ash

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Composition of Air? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Composition of Air.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Composition of Air.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Composition of Air.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Composition of Air.

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Change of State? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Change of State.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Change of State.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Change of State.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Change of State.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Slopes as simple machines and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Invertebrates and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Change of State and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Composition of Air and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. D — Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

2. D — Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

3. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Light.

4. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Levers as simple machines.

5. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Slopes as simple machines.

6. D — newton (N)

7. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Invertebrates.

8. B — 100 °C

9. B — Glucose and oxygen

10. C — Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

11. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Composition of Air.

12. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Change of State.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Slopes as simple machines; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Change of State; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Composition of Air; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
